数组的一个重要概念是: **数组名**作为一个**指针**已经指向数组的第一个元素。因此，语句`*ptr = a`等价于`*ptr = &a[0]`。

An important concept with arrays is that an array name acts as a pointer to the first element of the array. Therefore, the statement ptr = a can be thought of as ptr = &a[0]. Consider the following statement, which prints the first element of the array: printf("%d ", *a);

resolved.title: 更多地址运算
resolved.description:
[s0l0!-header][h1]More Address Arithmetic[/h1][/s0l0!-header] 

Address arithmetic can also be thought of as pointer arithmetic because the operations involve pointers.
Besides using + and – to refer to the next and previous memory locations, you can use the assignment operators to change the address the pointer contains.

[s0l0!-header][b]For example:[/b][/s0l0!-header] [code format="c" codeId="1710"]int a[5] = {22, 33, 44, 55, 66};
int *ptr = NULL;

ptr = a;  /* point to the first array element */
printf("%d  %x\n", *ptr, ptr);  /* 22 */
ptr++;
printf("%d  %x\n", *ptr, ptr);  /* 33 */
ptr += 3;
printf("%d  %x\n", *ptr, ptr);  /* 66 */
ptr--;
printf("%d  %x\n", *ptr, ptr);  /* 55 */
ptr -= 2;
printf("%d  %x\n", *ptr, ptr);  /* 33 */ [/code]
[s0l0!-header][b]Program output is similar to:[/b][/s0l0!-header] [code format="raw" ]22 febd4760
33 febd4764
66 febd4770
55 febd476c
33 febd4764 [/code]
When a pointer is incremented, the memory address increases by the number of bytes being pointed to. In the program above, the pointer increases by 4 when the increment operator is used (ptr++) because the pointer is pointing to an int.
[note]You can also use the ==, <, and > operators to compare pointer addresses.[/note]
